title: Fibre degree bounds hold for all field-valued points (Stacks 03J5)
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $n\ge0$ an integer. The following are equivalent: (1) $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]; (2) for every field $K$ and every morphism of schemes $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the fibre product $X_K=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product], regarded as a scheme over $K$ through its second projection $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, is finite over $K$ (the projection is a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]) and $\dim_K\Gamma(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})\le n$, where $\Gamma(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})$ is a $K$-algebra through the ring map induced by the projection.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15322, equivalence of (1) and (2), and the first two sentences of its proof (line 15339: (2)=>(1) trivial, taking Spec kappa(y) -> Y; (1)=>(2) since X_K = Spec K x_{Spec kappa(y)} X_y for y the image of Spec K -> Y)

proof.text: *(2)$\Rightarrow$(1).* Assume (2) and let $y\in Y$. Take $K=\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field] and for $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ the canonical morphism $j_y:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to Y$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] the fibre $X_y$ is the fibre product $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ of $f$ and $j_y$, regarded over $\kappa(y)$ through its second projection, and the $\kappa(y)$-algebra structure of $\Gamma(X_y,\mathcal O_{X_y})$ used in the degree [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound] is the one induced by that projection; this is exactly the scheme $X_K$ of (2) with its structure over $K$. (If $X_K$ is another choice of the fibre product, the unique isomorphism $u:X_K\to X_y$ of fibre products commutes with the second projections, so the projection of $X_y$ is that of $X_K$ composed with the isomorphism $u^{-1}$, finite by [lem-weil-pbc-isomorphism-finite] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], and $\Gamma(u)$ is an isomorphism of $\kappa(y)$-algebras, so finiteness and the dimension of global sections agree.) Hence (2) says that $X_y$ is finite over $\kappa(y)$ with $\dim_{\kappa(y)}\Gamma(X_y,\mathcal O_{X_y})\le n$. As $y$ was arbitrary, $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound].

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339, 'The implication (2) => (1) is trivial' (take the canonical Spec kappa(y) -> Y)

proof.text: *The point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$.* For the converse, let $K$ be a field and $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ a morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $K$ is a field, $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has exactly one point $\xi=(0)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] with $R=K$, $\mathfrak p=(0)$: the canonical morphism $j_\xi:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ of the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] equals $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ with $\varphi=e^{-1}\circ\pi:K\to\kappa(\xi)$, where $\pi:K\to K_{(0)}/(0)K_{(0)}$ and $e$ is a ring isomorphism. Every nonzero element of $K$ is a unit, so the localization $K\to K_{(0)}$ is an isomorphism, and the quotient by the zero ideal is an isomorphism; hence $\pi$ and $\varphi$ are isomorphisms of fields, and $j_\xi=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ is an isomorphism of schemes with inverse $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi^{-1})$. Under $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)=A$ the map induced by $j_\xi$ on global sections is $\varphi:K\to\kappa(\xi)$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339, second sentence (the field k of the point Spec(k) -> Y, written out)

proof.text: *(1)$\Rightarrow$(2): the base change of the fibre.* Assume (1); let $g$, $\xi$, $\varphi$ be as in step 2 and $y=g(\xi)$. Put $X_K=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K$ with projections $\mathrm{pr}_1:X_K\to X$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2:X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. By (1), the fibre $X_y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is finite over $\kappa(y)$ of degree $d=\dim_{\kappa(y)}\Gamma(X_y,\mathcal O_{X_y})\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-base-change] with $S=Y$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$, the morphisms $f$ and $g$, $X_T=X_K$, $f_T=\mathrm{pr}_2$, $t=\xi$ and $s=g(\xi)=y$: the fibre $F=(X_K)_\xi=X_K\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$ of $\mathrm{pr}_2$ at $\xi$ (fibre product of $\mathrm{pr}_2$ and $j_\xi$), with projections $p:F\to X_K$ and $q:F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$, $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ p=j_\xi\circ q$, is finite over $\kappa(\xi)$ (the morphism $q$ is finite) and $\dim_{\kappa(\xi)}\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_F)=d$, where $\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_F)$ is a $\kappa(\xi)$-algebra through $q$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339, 'The other implication holds because if the image of Spec(k) -> Y is y, then X_k = Spec(k) x_{Spec(kappa(y))} X_y' (degree preserved by the base change of fields)

proof.text: *$F$ is $X_K$.* Since $j_\xi$ is an isomorphism (step 2), $(X_K,\mathrm{id}_{X_K},j_\xi^{-1}\circ\mathrm{pr}_2)$ is a fibre product of $\mathrm{pr}_2$ and $j_\xi$ [def-pc-fibre-product]: it commutes, $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\mathrm{id}=j_\xi\circ(j_\xi^{-1}\circ\mathrm{pr}_2)$, and for a scheme $W$ with $a:W\to X_K$, $b:W\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$, $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ a=j_\xi\circ b$, the morphism $a$ is the unique $h:W\to X_K$ with $\mathrm{id}\circ h=a$, and it satisfies $j_\xi^{-1}\circ\mathrm{pr}_2\circ a=b$. By uniqueness of fibre products up to unique isomorphism, the first projection $p:F\to X_K$ is an isomorphism, and $q=j_\xi^{-1}\circ\mathrm{pr}_2\circ p$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339, second sentence, specialization of the base change to T = Spec(k), t its point (kappa(t) = k), written out

proof.text: *$X_K$ is finite over $K$.* By step 4, $\mathrm{pr}_2=j_\xi\circ q\circ p^{-1}$. The isomorphisms $p^{-1}$ and $j_\xi$ are finite [lem-weil-pbc-isomorphism-finite], $q$ is finite (step 3), and a composition of finite morphisms is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]; so $\mathrm{pr}_2:X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], i.e. $X_K$ is finite over $K$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339, second sentence ('X_k ... is finite over k'), written out

proof.text: *The degree of $X_K$.* Apply $\Gamma(-,\mathcal O)$ to $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ p=j_\xi\circ q$: with $\alpha:K\to\Gamma(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})$ and $\beta:\kappa(\xi)\to\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_F)$ the maps induced by $\mathrm{pr}_2$ and $q$ (the algebra structures of the degree), $p^*:\Gamma(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})\to\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_F)$ the ring isomorphism induced by the isomorphism $p$, and $\varphi$ the map induced by $j_\xi$ (step 2), we get $p^*\circ\alpha=\beta\circ\varphi$. So $p^*(\alpha(a)v)=\beta(\varphi(a))p^*(v)$: $p^*$ is a bijection, additive and semilinear along the field isomorphism $\varphi$, hence maps a $K$-basis of $\Gamma(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})$ onto a $\kappa(\xi)$-basis of $\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_F)$ and conversely. Therefore $\dim_K\Gamma(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})=\dim_{\kappa(\xi)}\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_F)=d\le n$ (step 3). Together with step 5 this is (2) for $g$; as $K$ and $g$ were arbitrary, (1) implies (2).
